Shivakumar Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday (November 14, 2026) asserted that Karnataka would go ahead with the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project, describing it as the State’s right and duty, while assuring that Tamil Nadu would receive its stipulated share of Cauvery water. Responding to opposition to the project from leaders in Tamil Nadu, including State Congress president Manickam Tagore, Mr. Shivakumar said the neighbouring State should send a delegation to Karnataka to understand the project’s benefits rather than oppose it. “Anyone is free to oppose it, but Tamil Nadu must recognise that this is our State and our right. If they wish, let them send a delegation. I am prepared to take them to the dam site and explain the project,” he told presspersons. ... #### Assam accident: Autopsy of 26 bodies on November 14; CM to visit injured, meet families of deceased The postmortem of the bodies of 26 people who died in a collision between a minibus and a container truck in Assam’s Kaziranga will be conducted on Saturday (November 14, 2026), Minister Ranoj Pegu said. The condition of seven of the 18 injured people remained critical, said Mr. Pegu, who was deputed by Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to visit the accident site and the hospitals where the injured are receiving treatment. Mr. Sarma is scheduled to visit the families of the deceased and the injured under treatment in hospitals in Golaghat district on Saturday and take stock of the situation. Twenty-six people died in a head-on collision between the two vehicles at Rangajan on National Highway 715 near Kaziranga National Park on Friday (Novembe 13, 2026). Many of the victims were college students who were returning from their classes. “The postmortem will be conducted at Swahid Kushal Konwar Civil Hospital in Golaghat, after which ambulances will take the bodies to their residence,” Mr. Pegu told reporters. ... #### Microsoft says services fully restored after hourslong global outage Microsoft said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that services were fully restored after a massive outage that lasted for hours. “We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the company said in an update on X. Users reported that Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories. The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had impacted some of their operations.

items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 14, 2026
items.excerpt: Merve Aydogan 14 November 2026• Update: 14 November 2026 HAMILTON, Canada Here's a rundown of all the news you need to know for Saturday, including Türkiye and Qatar signing five agreements, including a mutual defense pact, during the 12th meeting of the Türkiye-Qatar High Strategic Committee in Istanbul; the US Federal Aviation Administration lifting a nationwide flight ground stop after a telecommunications outage; and US President Donald Trump set to hold trilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen next week, according to the White House. Türkiye and Qatar signed five agreements, including a mutual defense pact, during the 12th meeting of the Türkiye-Qatar High Strategic Committee in Istanbul, with the signing ceremony held at the Presidential Dolmabahce Office in the presence of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani. Erdogan and Sheikh Tamim signed the mutual defense agreement, while the other deals cover consumer protection, education, and cooperation on peace, reconciliation and conflict resolution. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani signed the memorandum on peace, reconciliation and conflict resolution, along with a joint declaration marking the committee’s 12th meeting. - US FAA lifts nationwide flight ground stop after telecommunications outage The US Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop at airports after a telecommunications outage affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centers prompted authorities to halt flights as a precaution, with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy describing the problem as a "communication issue" and "an emergency." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that the public was "never" in danger and that there was "no indication as of yet that this was a nefarious attack." "We’re not ruling out anything," Mullin said when asked about a possible cyberattack, while the FAA said every flight had been accounted for and international flights would be handled case by case. Separately, Microsoft said it had "no indication" the ground stop was related to any of its services, while FlightAware said more than 10,000 flights were delayed or canceled. - Trump to hold trilateral talks with Xi, Putin in China next week: White House US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, with assistant White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales saying he will discuss reducing nuclear weapons, whose proliferation Trump believes is "very dangerous." A senior US official said Washington does not expect an agreement, calling the talks "the entry point, the first conversation" at the leader level, and said Trump plans to raise Iran but not Ukraine because China is not part of the separate US-Russia track. Trump will leave Washington on Monday for Manila for a Quad leaders’ meeting and the US-ASEAN Special Summit, then travel to Shenzhen on Wednesday, where he will hold a meeting and working lunch with Xi on Thursday before the trilateral meeting. Another senior US official described the Trump-Xi session as an "implementation check-in” on the trade agreement, with no tariff changes expected. Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk will join Trump for parts of his visit to China but will not participate in official meetings, according to US officials. ... - The Pan American Health Organization has revoked the US measles elimination status after outbreaks in several states and 5,400 cases reported in 2026, with health experts blaming low vaccination coverage.

items.title: Strong Growth, Rising Prices and a Fed Behind the Curve | The Daily Spark
items.excerpt: November 14, 2026 # Strong Growth, Rising Prices and a Fed Behind the Curve About the Author Torsten Slok Partner, Chief Economist October nonfarm payrolls and CPI were strong, the AI spending boom continues and the Atlanta Fed estimates fourth-quarter GDP growth at 3.5%, significantly above the 2% potential growth rate. At the same time, regional Fed surveys of prices paid, shifted six months forward, point to a continued strong uptrend in inflation, with PCE inflation moving towards 6%, see chart below. The bottom line is that strong demand, combined with ongoing supply shocks to imports, labor and energy, raises the risk that the Fed is falling behind the curve and will have to raise rates much more than markets currently expect.

items.title: Fed’s Jefferson says he is taking his policy cues from inflation By Reuters
items.excerpt: Nov 13 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on Friday that, with the economy growing and the labor market stabilized, he is taking his policy cues from inflation, a remark that suggests he may support further interest-rate hikes to bring it under control. Jefferson joined the 10-2 majority of Fed policymakers who voted at their October meeting to wait for more data to accumulate before considering a rate hike. "Data received since that meeting have been consistent with economic activity and labor market conditions remaining broadly solid, while inflation readings show persistent price pressures," Jefferson said in remarks prepared for delivery at the University of California, San Diego. "Accordingly, I see the trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal for determining the appropriate stance of monetary policy." Other Fed policymakers in recent weeks have been explicit that elevated and persistent inflation means they would likely support rate hikes that are bigger or come in quicker succession than the single quarter-point increase the Fed delivered in September. Jefferson gave no such guidance. "Going forward, I believe that further policy adjustments should be determined by carefully examining trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks," he said.

items.title: Wholesale food prices are on the rise
items.excerpt: Food prices are rising sharply even before they reach supermarket shelves. Why it matters: Americans are already paying more for groceries. New inflation data this week suggests that the pressure is not letting up. - Wholesale fresh and dry vegetable prices surged 27% last month, adding to a 31% price jump the previous month. - These are the prices paid by food distributors, grocery chains and other businesses to farmers and other producers for eventual sale to consumers. - Wholesale food prices overall are up 1.7% from a year earlier, ending a three-month streak of annual price declines. Zoom in: Unusually warm weather, crop disease and insect infestations have reduced lettuce and other leafy green harvests in California. - The Iran war, meanwhile, has driven up the cost of fertilizer and fuel, making it more expensive to grow and transport food. - A regional grocery chain recently told Federal Reserve officials that it now costs more to transport a head of lettuce from California than to buy the lettuce itself, citing high diesel fuel prices. - Truck freight costs are up almost 25% over the past year, the largest annual increase since 2022 and on par with the surge seen during the pandemic-era inflation shock. The big picture: It's unclear how much of the surge in producer prices will be passed along to consumers. But steeper price increases were already showing up at supermarket checkout counters last month. - Grocery prices rose 0.4%, the biggest monthly increase in 6 months, driven by higher prices for meat, dairy products and snack foods. - Fresh vegetable prices climbed 2%, including a nearly 8% jump in lettuce prices.

items.title: Bessent, Fed official divided on role of energy shock in inflation - Gulf Times
items.excerpt: Reuters/ Washington Published on November 14, 2026 | 12:00 AM US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. (file picture) US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday that the Federal Reserve should not hike rates because of inflation driven by an "energy supply shock" tied to the Iran war, comments made to CNBC and promptly contradicted on the network by Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, who said price pressures were building far beyond what could be explained by high oil prices. "I think the Fed should understand that this is an energy supply shock," while the underlying US economy is very strong, Bessent said in an interview on CNBC. "So I think that to hike too much into an energy supply shock when it's coming down, these are very noisy numbers...You know, the Fed's supposed to look into the future, not look in the rearview mirror." Shortly afterwards, the network hosted Goolsbee, a regular guest on CNBC's morning Squawk Box show, who said that inflation was not just due to energy, but had spread to the service sector and areas like medical care that are not usually responsive to the price of oil, and was also elevated through strong demand tied to the AI data centre buildout. "I respect the secretary and I am trying to figure out the same thing he is trying to figure out, which is how persistent is this inflation? The tariff inflation and oil price shock were supposed to have gone away by now and it hasn't," Goolsbee said. "One puzzle is why have those supply shocks been as persistent as they have been. A second thing is if demand is overheating and that is contributing to inflation, that is more worrisome... Services inflation, which is probably not coming from tariffs or oil, is one of the more troubling aspects of the inflation reports we have been getting." While not committing to a rate hike, he said the Fed "has definitely got work to do to continue to reestablish its credibility." The two interviews highlighted competing narratives about aspects of the US economy that figured heavily in midterm elections that centered on high inflation as well as the rapid pace of an AI buildout. The Trump administration has cheered the AI boom and focused on the likely upside, while being critical of communities ... Fed policymakers were open to the possibility they could "look through" supply-driven inflation at the start of the US war with Iran. But as inflation remained lodged above the Fed's target, concern about it grew, as did support for rate hikes. Research meanwhile opened a different window on the relationship between oil prices and US inflation. Because the US is an energy exporter, higher global oil prices can filter through to the economy in the form of higher corporate profits and wages, providing a source of inflation beyond supply issues that can't be easily ignored by the central bank. Recent stronger-than-expected jobs and inflation reports have further bolstered the case for more Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, and even prompted some officials to discuss the need for a larger-than-typical half-percentage-point increase at the central bank's coming December 8-9 meeting. "We have had signs of trouble now for several months in a row if you look at how broad-based the inflation is," Goolsbee said. "In categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you are still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way ... That is not going away no matter what happens to the price of oil." "Are we on a path back to 2%? My feeling right now is we are not and we've got to deal with that," Goolsbee said. "Conventional wisdom says do everything you can to prevent demand overheating," Goolsbee said, with coming data on inflation the key to whether the Fed needs a faster pace of rate increases.

items.title: Goolsbee Says Broader Inflation Could Prompt a Tougher Fed Response | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: By Miriam Hart Nov 14, 2026, 9:50 AM UTC ... Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Friday that worsening inflation data could require a more forceful Federal Reserve response, as U.S. policymakers assess whether price pressures are spreading beyond energy. Goolsbee made the remarks in a Nov. 13 interview on CNBC’s Squawk Box, which the Chicago Fed lists on its media appearances page. He said inflation had reached categories not driven by energy. His response was conditional on incoming data, and he did not commit to a rate increase. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported that the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, after a 0.6% increase in September. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3% month over month in August, September and October. Because the BLS did not collect October 2025 data during the lapse in appropriations, it could not publish 12-month changes for most CPI series. EconoTimes previously covered October’s CPI report and Goolsbee’s comments on services inflation. Producer prices also rose. The BLS said its final-demand Producer Price Index (PPI) increased 0.3% in October and 6.5% over the 12 months through October. That annual increase was the largest since November 2022, when it was 7.4%. The CPI figures provide monthly comparisons, while the missing October 2025 data prevent most annual comparisons in the latest consumer-price release. The Fed’s longer-run inflation goal is 2%, measured using annual changes in the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index. On Oct. 28, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) kept its federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4.00%; two members preferred a quarter-point increase. Minutes from the Oct. 27-28 meeting are due Nov. 18. The FOMC’s next meeting is scheduled for Dec. 8-9, and the BLS is scheduled to release November CPI data Dec. 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET.

items.title: Ebenezer Box Office: Johnny Depp Movie Leads on Opening Day
items.excerpt: Nov 14, 2026 8:05am PT # Box Office: Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Leads With $6.7 Million on Opening Day, ‘How to Rob a Bank’ Struggling With $2.2 Million on Friday By Rebecca Rubin Senior Film and Media Reporter ... “ Ebenezer,” an adaptation of “A Christmas Carol” starring Johnny Depp as Scrooge, led the box office on Friday with $6.7 million on opening day. The PG-13 take on the Charles Dickens classic is projected to earn $18 million to $20 million from 3,535 North American theaters in its opening weekend. “Ebenezer” should bring in another $20 million overseas for a global tally around $38 million to $40 million. That would represent a solid start because Paramount spent a modest $38 million to produce the film. Audiences awarded the movie an “A-” grade on CinemaScore exit polls. Directed by Ti West, known for the “X” horror trilogy, “Ebenezer” spins the oft-told tale of the curmudgeonly businessman who is visited by the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future. “Ebenezer” is notable as Depp’s first major movie in eight years, since 2018’s “Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald.” ... Another newcomer, Sony’s action thriller “Ghost Soldier,” starring Jim Caviezel as a former American Special Forces soldier, grossed $1.5 million from 2,558 locations on Friday. It’s expected to generate $4.9 million during the traditional weekend and $8 million over its first five days of release. It was produced for $18 million. This weekend’s other new release, Amazon MGM’s “ How to Rob a Bank,” is fizzling with $2.2 million from 2,810 theaters on Friday. The heist comedy, starring Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz and Pete Davidson, is pacing to open to just $4.75 million. That’s not promising considering the studio produced the movie for more than $40 million, and theater owners keep about half of ticket sales. David Leitch directed the R-rated caper, which follows a crew of social media-savvy bank robbers who broadcast their daring heists, unaware their viral fame has caught the attention of the feds. “How to Rob a Bank” landed a “B-” grade on CinemaScore exit polls and tepid 33% from critics on Rotten Tomatoes. “How to Rob a Bank” placed third on Friday, but it’s bracing for No. 7 on weekend box office charts behind several holdovers, including Warner Bros. Animation’s “The Cat in the Hat” and Gkids’ “Godzilla Minus Zero.” At No. 2, “The Cat in the Hat” brought in $2.2 million on Friday and looks to generate $10 million by Sunday, a 50% decline from its debut. Those ticket sales would take the domestic total to $36.7 million, a weak tally against a $92 million budget. “Godzilla Minus Zero” wasn’t far behind with $2.1 million on Friday. The kaiju sequel should collect $7.5 million in its second weekend, a harsh 75% drop from its opening. Still, “Godzilla Minus Zero” has been a hit in North America. Those returns will bring the Stateside haul to $48.1 million.

items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 14 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: ## Trailers and first looks Sony Pictures Classics has released the official US teaser trailer for Iron Boy, Louis Clichy’s hand-drawn animated feature and winner of the Special Jury Prize in Un Certain Regard at Cannes. The film opens in limited release on 4 December 2026, with a nationwide release on 22 January 2027. Keerthy Suresh plays Savithiri, a lawyer fighting to save her husband, in the trailer for Sathyavan Savithiri, out now ahead of the film’s 20 November 2026 theatrical release. Mysskin plays a major part. Bhuvan Bam is back as Titu Mama in the Dhindora season 2 trailer, with Sanjeeda Sheikh joining the cast as Kavita Mami. The new season premieres on Netflix on 20 November 2026. A young man who moves to Kathmandu to change his life after being unable to succeed in his studies is the subject of Gobar Ganesh, whose trailer is out. The Nepali film is directed by Marichman Shrestha and stars Balchhi and Barsha Siwakoti. It reaches cinemas on Magh 1. Dhiraaj Rajbanshi’s Himalayan Gold has a second trailer out, ahead of its 20 November 2026 cinema release. Sunil Thapa, Karma, Parikshya Limbu and Rahul Mukhia star. Dhanush and Mammootty share the screen for the first time in the OM: Chapter 1 trailer, out now. Rajkumar Periasamy directs, and the film opens in theatres worldwide on 20 November 2026. Christopher Briney and Michelle Randolph star in Clashing Through the Snow, whose first trailer is out. The holiday road-trip romantic comedy, directed by Carlson Young, premieres on Prime Video on 23 November 2026. The 1960 plot to assassinate Fidel Castro during his United Nations visit is the subject of Killing Castro, whose official trailer Lionsgate has released. Produced by Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson and DJ Khaled, it opens in cinemas on 11 December 2026 and arrives on digital on 18 December. D Gukesh, R Praggnanandhaa, R Vaishali, Arjun Erigaisi and Vidit Gujrathi are the subjects of CANDIDATES, a six-episode series whose official trailer Dopamine Media has released. It premieres on the Dopamine Media YouTube channel on 22 November 2026. ## Casting and production Cristiano Ronaldo has begun production on Day 1s, his first television show. The scripted drama follows a fictional elite football agency and comes from UR-Marv, with Ronaldo executive producing and expected to make his acting debut. No platform or release date has been announced. School Spirits has confirmed its season 4 cast, with 12 stars returning and one promoted to series regular. Christian Weissmann, Katharine Isabella, Clara Alexandrova and Briana Buckmaster join as guest stars, and production is under way. Vishwambhara, Chiranjeevi’s fantasy adventure known during production as Mega 156, has begun its regular shoot. The film is directed by Vassishta and produced by UV Creations, and is billed as the costliest film of Chiranjeevi’s career. Isla Fisher and Blake Ritson have joined Al Pacino in Captivated, Dito Montiel’s thriller about the kidnapping of John Paul Getty III, with Jackson Kelly also joining the cast. Production is under way in Calabria and Rome in Italy. Apple TV has promoted Samba Schutte to series regular for Pluribus season 2. His Mr. Diabate returns with an expanded presence after two guest episodes in season 1. No premiere date has been announced. Netflix has announced Pushpak Vimaan, a crime-caper comedy series from Sudip Sharma starring Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhishek Banerjee and Barun Sobti. No premiere date was given with the announcement. Kai Cech is to voice Shanti in Lost in Mandala, the first global animated feature from Nepal’s Incessant Rain Studios. The film is directed by former Disney visual effects supervisor Kiran Bhakta Joshi, with a screenplay by Zack Stentz, and is now in pre-production with no release date announced. MobLand season 3 starts production next week. Helen Mirren confirmed the start on the A Talent for Murder red carpet, with Tom Hardy and Pierce Brosnan returning. The season 2 finale airs on 20 November 2026. Freya Allan is to lead System, a horror film from director Joachim Ronning. Filming is under way in abandoned London Underground stations and tunnels, with Denzel Baidoo and Felix Edwards co-starring. ## Box office and streaming Ramayana: Rise of a Legend has crossed $100 million worldwide in seven days, with Rs 944.55 crore reported by Sacnilk. CNBC TV18 reports it as the first film outside China to reach the mark in 2026. The Kannada dubbed version of Ramayana: Part 1 has crossed Rs 50 crore net in India, the first Bollywood film to do so. It took Rs 48.95 crore in its eight-day opening week plus Rs 1.17 crore on day 9, and the Karnataka gross across all languages has passed Rs 100 crore. Paper Tiger has debuted at 85 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 114 reviews. The James Gray crime drama stars Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson, and opened in limited release on 13 November 2026. Hulu has set 13 January 2027 as the premiere date for The Spot, an A24 psychological thriller starring Claire Danes and Ewan McGregor as a surgeon and her schoolteacher husband who suspect she caused a child’s hit-and-run death. First-look images were released on 12 November 2026. ... Christian Cousins, who played Dominic Palmieri in Kindergarten Cop alongside his twin brother Joseph, has died aged 43. He also played Bobby Gibson in Knots Landing. He died in October 2026, his brother Jonas Roeser announced on Instagram, saying Cousins had been very sick with liver disease.
